items.q: How much of an atom is empty space?
items.correct: Almost all of it — the mass is concentrated in a tiny central nucleus.
items.misconception: An atom is a solid sphere with no empty space.
items.random_wrong: An atom is made only of electrons.
items.why: Most of an atom's volume is empty; nearly all its mass sits in the nucleus.

items.q: Where are the electrons in an atom?
items.correct: In shells (energy levels) around the nucleus.
items.misconception: Inside the nucleus alongside the protons.
items.random_wrong: Spread evenly throughout the whole atom as a solid.
items.why: The nucleus holds protons and neutrons; electrons occupy shells around it.

items.q: What decides which element an atom is?
items.correct: Its number of protons (the atomic number).
items.random_wrong: Its number of electrons, even in an ion.
items.why: Proton number fixes the element; neutron number varies (isotopes) and electron number changes in ions.

items.q: How do a compound's properties compare with its elements?
items.correct: They are different — bonding gives the compound new properties.
items.misconception: They are the same as the elements it is made from.
items.random_wrong: A compound can be separated by filtering.
items.why: Sodium (reactive metal) + chlorine (toxic gas) form salt; compounds need chemical reactions to break apart.
